title: Objection Handling - LAER
subtitle: A prospect raises an objection and you immediately counter it with a feature or a price
useWhen: justification. They feel unheard, push back harder, and the conversation dies. You're winning arguments and losing deals.
howToUse: Developed by Carew International, the LAER model is a four-step objection response framework built on one principle: an objection is a request for more information, not an attack to defend against. Listen (fully, without interrupting), Acknowledge (validate their concern before responding), Explore (ask a question to understand the objection more deeply), and Respond (only now address it with precision). Skipping Explore is the most common mistake. Most objections have a deeper concern underneath the surface one.
steps: Never respond to an objection in the same breath you heard it, pause.
Acknowledge before you explore - validation opens people, defence closes them.
Use the Explore question to find what is really underneath the objection.

Prepare LAER responses for your top 5 most common objections using the prompt below. Turn resistance into a deeper conversation, not a debate 'We need to think about it' is never about thinking. It is always about one of three things: they don't see enough value, they don't have authority, or they don't have urgency. The Explore question reveals which one it is. Without that question, you're responding to the wrong problem. PRO TIP
origin: Carew International — LAER objection handling methodology
promptBody:
Act as a sales coach using the LAER objection handling framework.
My product  :  [WHAT YOU SELL AND AVERAGE PRICE POINT]
For each objection below, write a full LAER response:
Objection 1  :  [YOUR MOST COMMON OBJECTION]
Objection 2  :  [YOUR SECOND MOST COMMON OBJECTION]
Objection 3  :  'We don't have budget right now.'
Objection 4 :  'We need to think about it.'
Objection 5 :  'We're already using [COMPETITOR].'
For each objection use this structure:
LISTEN                  :  (note what to observe / not interrupt)
ACKNOWLEDGE :  Exact words to validate their concern
EXPLORE              :  One open question to uncover the real issue
RESPOND             :  Precise response to the likely real concern
LAER — Turn Objections Into Conversations
Listen
Acknowledge
Explore
Respond
The most expensive STP mistake is targeting the largest segment instead of the
most winnable one. A smaller segment where you have a clear advantage will
outperform a large segment where you are one of many.
